propers.text:
Deus, qui infirmitati nostrae ad terendam salutis viam in Sanctis tuis
exemplum et praesidium collocasti: da nobis, ita beati Gulielmi Abbatis

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 fills the Common's N. placeholder with the saint's proper name, because the only 1862 occurrence of this Secret is in a sanctoral Abbot's Mass; the 1922 Mame prints the placeholder; the 1862 opening word carried by an ornamental initial; the scan's recogniser loses it (target opens altaribus domine hostias); cue or word lost at the edge of the aligned window (target n, the 1862 layer ioannes); recogniser damage, same word: target reads quesumus, the 1862 layer reads qua sumus; recogniser damage, same word: target reads prouenire, the 1862 layer reads proueirire; conclusion length: the 1862 prints the short printed cue where the 1962 writes the conclusion out. Corroboration: 1922 Mame, artifact PDF p. 911 (printed p. 33* of the Commune Sanctorum); read from the page's word bounding boxes, reflowed column by column; reading: AcRIS altaribus, Domine, S hostias superpositas sanctus N. Abbas, quesumus, in salutem nobis provenire deposcat. Per Déminum,. Recorded limitation: The 1862 does not print this Secret in its own short Missa pro Abbatibus, which gives the Collect only; it prints the same Secret verbatim in a sanctoral Abbot's Mass, with the saint's name standing where the Common prints the placeholder N. The 1922 Mame prints it in its own Commune Abbatum with the placeholder, and that reading was read off the Mame's column-correct page text, not inferred. Target reading settled on the CMAA facsimile page image at 450 dpi; the crops read are kept in .scratch/backfill/commons-2/work/img. Not checked: the 1862's own page images, which this repository holds only for printed pp. [31], [32], [37] and [52]-[56].
